name: call_library_vector_keep_d0
description: Calls a routine through a function pointer at a fixed negative offset from a base value kept in a global, then returns the D0 value unchanged. It is part of libs/mathtrans.library, is referenced from the library's data, and is called by one other routine.

name: call_library_vector_keep_d0
description: Calls a routine through a function pointer at a fixed negative offset from a global base value and returns the D0 value unchanged. It is part of libs/mathtrans.library and is referenced from the library's data table.

name: call_library_vector_return_pair
description: Calls a routine through a function pointer at a fixed negative offset from a global base value and returns D0 and D1 together as one 64-bit result. It is part of libs/mathtrans.library and is referenced from the library's data table.

name: call_library_vector_return_pair
description: Calls a routine through a function pointer held in a global base table and returns the D0 and D1 results together as a 64-bit value. It is part of libs/mathtrans.library and is referenced from its data.

name: call_library_vector_keep_d0
description: Calls a routine through a function pointer at a fixed negative offset from a global base and returns the D0 value unchanged. It is part of libs/mathtrans.library and is referenced from the library's data table.

name: call_library_vector_keep_d0
description: Calls a routine through a function pointer at a fixed negative offset from a global base and returns D0 unchanged. It is part of libs/mathtrans.library and is referenced from the library's data.

name: call_library_vector_return_pair
description: Calls a routine through a function pointer in a global base table and returns D0 and D1 together as a 64-bit value. It is part of libs/mathtrans.library, is referenced from data, and is called by five other routines.

name: call_library_vector_return_pair
description: Calls a routine through a function pointer in a global base table and returns D0 and D1 together as a 64-bit value. It is part of libs/mathtrans.library, is referenced from data, and is called by six other routines.

name: call_library_vector_return_pair
description: Calls a routine through a function pointer in a global base table and returns D0 and D1 together as a 64-bit value. It is part of libs/mathtrans.library, is referenced from data, and is called by five other routines.

name: call_library_vector_return_pair
description: Calls a routine through a function pointer held in a global base table and returns D0 and D1 together as one 64-bit value. It is part of libs/mathtrans.library, is referenced from data, and is called by ten other routines.

name: call_vector_offset_keep_d0
description: Calls a routine whose address is a global base plus an offset passed in A0, then returns the D0 value unchanged. It is part of libs/mathtrans.library and is called by four other routines.

name: normalize_fixed_point_value
description: Normalizes the signed 32-bit value in D6: it takes the magnitude, swaps the two 16-bit halves when the magnitude is small, then shifts left one bit at a time while counting down until the top bit is set or the count wraps. It is part of libs/mathtrans.library and is called by four other routines.

name: store_argument_in_block
description: Calls a library function through the library base; if it returns a non-null block, stores the A0 argument into a fixed field of that block and calls a second library function. It returns whether a block was obtained, and it is the first routine in libs/diskfont.library.

name: store_argument_in_block
description: Calls a library function through the library base; if it returns a non-null block, stores the A0 argument into a fixed field of that block and calls a second library function. It returns whether a block was obtained, and is part of libs/diskfont.library.

name: open_libraries_init_list
description: Opens two libraries through the exec library base, and if both succeed initializes an empty list header inside the supplied structure and returns that structure. If either open fails it calls a cleanup routine and returns zero; the dos.library and graphics.library names in the data show which libraries are opened.

name: close_library_and_free_block
description: Closes a library through a stored library pointer, frees a memory block with a second call through the same library base, and returns zero. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by one other routine.

name: release_unused_list_entries
description: Walks a linked list and unlinks every entry whose count field is not positive, releasing each one through a library call and decrementing the list's count. When the list is empty and an owner flag is clear it closes two libraries, frees the structure and returns its stored value; otherwise it sets a high flag bit and returns zero.

name: free_entry_when_idle
description: When the entry's owner flag is clear and its count is not positive, it closes two libraries, frees the entry, unlinks it from its list and returns the value stored in it. Otherwise it sets the entry's high flag bit and returns zero.

name: set_entry_flag_high_bit
description: Sets the top bit of a flag byte at a fixed field of the structure and returns zero, calling nothing else. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by one other routine.

name: clear_flag_and_increment_counter
description: Clears the top bit of a flag byte in the structure and increments a 16-bit counter in another field, with no return value. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is referenced from its data table.

name: decrement_count_and_finalize
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter in the structure and, when it reaches zero with the high flag bit set, calls a library routine through the library base and returns its result, otherwise returning zero. It is referenced from the library's data table.

name: scan_font_entries_into_buffer
description: Fills a caller-supplied buffer with fixed-size records describing linked-list entries, copying each entry's name and fields and counting the records in the first word, and a second flag bit also queries further entries through library calls. It is part of libs/diskfont.library.

name: append_list_entries_to_buffer
description: Loops over a linked list, copying each entry's name and fields into a caller buffer as a fixed-size record and incrementing the record count, then continues with library queries when a flag bit is set. It is part of libs/diskfont.library.

name: scan_name_string_into_records
description: Walks a character string one byte at a time and, at the end of each name, writes a record for the current list entry into the buffer and advances to the next entry, using the same library query path when a flag bit is set. It is part of libs/diskfont.library.

name: scan_fonts_directory_entries
description: Copies a path string that names the FONTS: directory into a buffer and walks it through the dos library's lock, examine and current-directory calls, allocating memory through exec and storing a record for each entry found. It is part of libs/diskfont.library.

name: scan_font_files_for_records
description: Walks a linked list of directory entries and, for names whose dot extension matches the .font suffix, opens the file, reads its header and appends a record for each entry. It is part of libs/diskfont.library.

name: parse_font_entry_records
description: Parses name strings from the current directory entry and, for each record read from the file, appends a fixed-size record to the output buffer, then closes the file. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by one other routine.

name: read_font_entries_from_file
description: Copies name bytes into a buffer while using the dos library read call to fill records from the file, appending each parsed entry to the output buffer. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by one other routine.

name: scan_directory_entries_with_cleanup
description: Iterates over directory entries through the dos scan calls, appending matching entry records to the buffer, and at the end closes, unlocks and frees the scan state, returning a count derived from the last result. It is called by three other routines.

name: return_zero_stub
description: A do-nothing stub that returns zero and touches no registers, memory or hardware. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by one other routine.

name: compute_position_flag_score
description: Computes a signed score from two records: it takes the difference of a 16-bit field in each, scales it by a fixed shift, then subtracts a table value for each of seven bit positions where the two flag bytes differ. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by three other routines.

name: accumulate_flag_bit_differences
description: Starts from a precomputed value and subtracts a table entry for each of seven bit positions where the two records' flag bytes differ. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by two other routines.

name: accumulate_flag_difference_tail
description: Continues a seven-step loop over bit positions of two flag bytes, subtracting a table entry for each position where the bits differ, and returns the running total. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by one other routine.

name: subtract_flag_terms_from_total
description: Runs a seven-step loop over bit positions of two flag bytes, subtracting table entries from a running total wherever a flag bit is set, and returns the total. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by one other routine.

name: return_constant_value
description: Returns a fixed constant without reading arguments or registers, and touches no memory. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by two other routines.

name: lookup_or_open_font_record
description: Copies the requested font name and attributes from its argument and looks them up through a library call, returning the match when one exists. Otherwise it searches the font records and opens the font through the graphics library; it is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by one other routine.

name: lock_fonts_directory_for_scan
description: Locks the FONTS: directory through the dos library, then looks up and examines its first entry through the same calls, storing the results in the scan state. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by one other routine.

name: examine_font_entries_into_records
description: Examines each directory entry in the scan state through the dos calls, reads a small header, allocates a buffer through exec for matching font data, and fills in font records. It calls several library stubs and is part of libs/diskfont.library.

name: select_best_scoring_record
description: Scores every record in a table of fixed-size font records with a comparison routine and picks the record with the highest score, then processes that record through library calls. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by one other routine.

name: add_best_scoring_font_entry
description: Finds the highest scoring record in the table, then adds it to the font list under forbid and permit protection, loading its segment and linking it through the dos, exec and graphics calls. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by one other routine.

name: unload_font_and_release_state
description: Clears a field of the current font record, unloads a segment through the dos call inside a loop, and releases the scan state before returning a value taken from a stored result. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by one other routine.

name: close_font_scan_and_release
description: Clears a field in the current font record and walks the records, then closes the file and directory handles and frees the scan state through the dos, exec and graphics calls. It returns a stored value and is called by five other routines.

name: create_font_record_from_name
description: Takes a font file name and its length, allocates a record through exec, copies the name into a path buffer, strips the extension and looks up the matching entry in the FONTS: directory through dos calls. It returns the new record and is part of libs/diskfont.library.

name: build_font_table_block
description: Counts the records in a list, allocates one block sized for those records plus a header through exec, fills in the header and count, then copies each record's entries into it while scanning the directory through dos calls. It returns the table block, and is part of libs/diskfont.library.

name: free_memory_from_stack_slot
description: Reads a stack argument and passes it, with its stack address, to the exec FreeMem stub to release a memory block. It returns nothing and is part of libs/diskfont.library.

name: copy_null_terminated_string
description: Copies bytes from a source string to a destination until the zero terminator has been copied. It is library code called by four other routines.

name: append_null_terminated_string
description: Moves to the end of the destination string and passes that end pointer and the source to the string copy routine, which appends the source. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by one other routine.

name: advance_to_terminator_and_call
description: Advances a pointer until it reaches the zero terminator of a string and then calls another routine with that pointer. It does no other work and is called by one other routine.

name: measure_string_length
description: Walks a zero-terminated string counting its bytes, not including the terminator, and returns the count. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by one other routine.

name: count_null_terminated_bytes
description: Advances through a zero-terminated byte sequence, adding one to the starting value in D0 for each byte including the terminator, and returns the total. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by one other routine.

name: compare_null_terminated_strings
description: Compares two zero-terminated strings byte by byte, returning minus one if the first is smaller at the first difference, one if it is larger, and zero when they match. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by two other routines.

name: compare_strings_in_registers
description: Compares the zero-terminated string at one address register with the string at the other, returning zero on a match, minus one when the first is smaller and one when it is larger. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by one other routine.

name: compare_strings_in_registers
description: Compares two zero-terminated strings held in address registers byte by byte, returning minus one, one, or zero on a match. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by two other routines.

name: find_byte_in_string
description: Scans a zero-terminated string for a given byte and returns a pointer to its first occurrence, or null if it is absent. It is part of libs/diskfont.library.

name: find_byte_in_string_registers
description: Scans forward from a string pointer for a byte held in a register, returning a pointer to the match or null when the zero terminator comes first. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by one other routine.

name: find_next_byte_after_pointer
description: Steps past the current byte and scans forward for the byte in a register, returning a pointer to the match or null if the terminator is reached first. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by two other routines.

name: find_last_byte_in_string
description: Measures a string's length and scans backward from its end for a given byte, returning a pointer to its last occurrence or null when none is found. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by three other routines.

name: scan_backward_for_byte
description: Scans backward from a pointer toward a lower limit for a byte held in a register, returning a pointer to the first match or null if the limit is passed. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by one other routine.

name: scan_backward_bounded_for_byte
description: Steps backward from a pointer and checks the limit before each comparison, returning a pointer to the byte held in a register or null when the limit is passed. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by two other routines.

name: skip_past_path_separator
description: Finds the first slash in a path string, or failing that the first colon, and returns a pointer just past it; if neither is present it returns the original pointer. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by two other routines.

name: increment_returned_value
description: Returns the value passed in D0 plus one, touching nothing else. It is part of libs/diskfont.library and is called by one other routine.

name: forward_call_without_arguments
description: Calls another routine with no arguments and returns, doing nothing else. It is one of the handler entries in libs/diskfont.library's data and is referenced from there.

name: forward_call_without_arguments
description: Calls another routine with no arguments and returns, doing nothing else. It is one of the handler entries in libs/diskfont.library's data and is referenced from there.

name: forward_call_without_arguments
description: Calls another routine with no arguments and returns, doing nothing else. It is one of the handler entries in libs/diskfont.library's data and is referenced from there.

name: forward_call_without_arguments
description: Calls another routine with no arguments and returns, doing nothing else. It is one of the handler entries in libs/diskfont.library's data and is referenced from there.

name: run_program_entry_sequence
description: Program entry point for the WORMS file that runs a sequence of calls, calls a routine through a global pointer that the facts identify as a memory release, clears a longword just below a pointer, and returns the D0 and D1 pair. It also calls a short countdown routine.

name: decrement_word_until_minus_one
description: Repeatedly decrements a 16-bit value in D6 until it wraps to minus one, then returns. It is called by one other routine.

name: find_max_and_prepare_buffer
description: Walks a linked list of values to find the largest stored field, then fills a table with a sequence of values that rise by two per entry, starting from a constant. It is part of the HDWORM file and calls several routines.

name: store_two_library_results
description: Clears a flag byte before each of two library calls and stores each returned word into a fixed global slot. It is part of the HDWORM file, calls three routines, and is called by one other routine.

name: call_three_routines_return_zero
description: Calls three other routines in sequence and returns zero. It is a handler entry in the HDWORM file and is referenced from its data.

name: store_four_call_results
description: Calls four routines in turn and stores each returned value into its own fixed global slot. It is part of the HDWORM file and is called by one other routine.

name: allocate_memory_with_offset
description: Calls the exec AllocMem stub; if the allocation returns a non-zero address it returns that address plus a fixed bias, otherwise zero. It is part of the HDWORM file and is called by one other routine.

name: call_free_memory_stub
description: Calls the exec FreeMem stub through the library base and returns, doing nothing else. It is part of the HDWORM file and is called by one other routine.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Returns zero without touching anything else. It is part of the HDWORM file and is referenced from its data.

name: retry_open_library_until_success
description: Repeatedly calls the exec OpenLibrary stub through the library base until it returns a non-zero handle, then returns. The file's data refers to dos.library, and it is called by one other routine.

name: call_close_library_stub
description: Calls the exec CloseLibrary stub through the library base and returns. It is part of the HDWORM file and is called by one other routine.

name: forward_call_without_arguments
description: Calls another routine with no arguments and returns, doing nothing else. It is part of the HDWORM file and is called by one other routine.

name: copy_byte_buffer
description: Copies a block of bytes from a source to a destination, moving eight bytes per iteration and then the remaining bytes one at a time. It is part of the HDWORM file and is called by one other routine.

name: reset_two_globals_and_call
description: Clears two global words to zero, calls another routine between them, and returns. It is part of the HDWORM file and is called by one other routine.

name: repeat_call_until_zero_flag
description: Calls another routine repeatedly until the zero condition flag is set, then returns. It is part of the HDWORM file and is called by two other routines.

name: allocate_and_link_block
description: Calls the exec allocation stub through the library base and, if it succeeds, links the new block at the head of a global list and returns a pointer just past its header; on failure it calls another routine. It is called by one other routine.

name: free_or_allocate_list_block
description: Searches a global linked list for the block passed in and, when found, unlinks and frees it through the exec free stub; when no block matches and a counter word is zero, it sets the counter and tries to allocate and link a new block. It calls one other routine.

name: find_list_tail
description: Follows a linked list through its next pointers until it reaches the null entry, then stores the address of the last node in a global word. It is part of the HDWORM file and is called by two other routines.

name: save_call_restore_global
description: Saves a global word, calls two other routines, and then restores the global to its saved value. It is part of the HDWORM file and is called by one other routine.

name: save_call_restore_global
description: Saves a global word, calls two other routines, and then restores the global to its saved value. It is part of the HDWORM file and is referenced from its data.

name: allocate_and_link_block
description: Calls the exec allocation stub through the library base and, if it succeeds, links the new block at the head of a global list and returns a pointer just past its header; on failure it calls another routine. It is part of the HDWORM file and is called by two other routines.

name: free_or_allocate_list_block
description: Searches a global linked list for the block passed in and, when found, unlinks and frees it through the exec free stub; when no block matches and a counter word is zero, it sets the counter and tries to allocate and link a new block. It calls one other routine and is called by three other routines.

name: free_matching_list_block
description: Walks a global linked list to the entry preceding the block passed in, unlinks that block and frees it through the exec free stub; when the list ends without a match it sets a counter word and allocates a new block if the counter was zero. It is called by one other routine.

name: allocate_list_head_block
description: Allocates a block through the exec allocation stub and pushes it onto the head of a global list, clearing its second word; on failure it calls another routine. It is part of the HDWORM file and is called by one other routine.

name: free_all_list_blocks
description: Removes the head entry from a global list and frees it, then frees each block in the chain that hangs from that entry, using the exec free stub. It is part of the HDWORM file and is called by three other routines.

name: compute_max_and_fill_table
description: Computes the largest value stored in a linked list and writes it into a table entry, then fills the following table words with a sequence that rises by two per entry, making further setup calls. It is part of the HDWORM file and is called by three other routines.

name: copy_sixteen_words_and_call
description: If the destination pointer is non-null, copies a fixed block of words from the base area into it, then calls another routine through the global base. It is part of the HDWORM file and is called by one other routine.

name: return_minus_one_stub
description: Returns minus one without touching registers or memory and calls nothing else. It is a runtime entry reached during the reference run.

name: open_libraries_and_copy_table
description: Opens libraries through the exec OldOpenLibrary call and, if the opens succeed, copies a block of words from a fixed source area into memory before calling further library routines. It was reached during the reference run.

name: open_libraries_and_copy_table
description: Opens libraries through the exec OldOpenLibrary call and, if the opens succeed, copies a block of words from a fixed source area into memory. It then calls allocation, library and close routines, and was reached during the reference run.

name: examine_unrecovered_routine
description: The decompiler could not produce pseudo-code for this three-instruction routine, so its behaviour cannot be recovered from the evidence. It is address-taken, is called by one other routine, and sits in a runtime segment.

name: copy_sixteen_words_and_call
description: If the destination pointer is non-null, copies a fixed block of words from a base-relative area into it, then calls another routine through the global base. It is part of the c/mem file and is called by one other routine.

name: load_trilogy_data_file
description: Program entry for the hardware.default file: it forbids multitasking, opens the dos library, and then either clears a block of memory or opens, reads and closes the TRILOGY.1 data file through the dos calls. It calls three other routines.

name: copy_words_into_strided_table
description: Copies thirty-two words from a source area into a table whose entries are four bytes apart, then calls library routines through the library base twice in sequence. It is referenced from data and is called by two other routines.

name: set_copper_list_pointers
description: Uses the dos open, read and close calls and the exec library open and close calls, then stores the low and high halves of a series of addresses into a list and writes the copper list location and jump registers. It refers to the TRILOGY.2 and TRILOGY.3 files and graphics.library.

name: poll_frame_and_enable_dma
description: Loops while a status bit is set, waiting on a counter and copying seven table entries, then touches the CIA port and the DMA control and vertical position registers. It calls the exec Permit and CloseLibrary routines and calls three other routines.

name: expand_byte_table_stream
description: Reads input bytes and, for each byte, uses an eight-byte entry of a lookup table in the global area to produce output bytes in a buffer, counting bit positions as it goes. It is called by one other routine.

name: expand_byte_table_with_mask
description: Reads input bytes and, for each byte, uses an eight-byte entry of a lookup table in the global area to produce output bytes, applying a bit mask at each step. It is called by one other routine.

name: expand_byte_table_with_mask
description: Reads input bytes and, for each byte, uses an eight-byte entry of a lookup table in the global area to produce output bytes, applying a bit mask at each step. It is referenced from data and is called by one other routine.

name: shift_bit_rows_left_one
description: Shifts a series of rows, each ten longwords wide, left by one bit across the row, carrying the top bit of each following longword into the one before, and repeats for the row count. It is called by one other routine.

name: shift_bit_rows_left_one
description: Shifts a series of rows, each ten longwords wide, left by one bit across the row, carrying the top bit of each following longword into the one before, and repeats for the row count. It is referenced from data and is called by two other routines.

name: repack_bit_stream_into_words
description: Walks a bit stream one bit at a time, shifting bits out of one longword sequence and into another, and writes a result word after every ten bits until the count runs out. It is called by one other routine.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Program entry stub that calls one other routine. The rest of its decoded body is bad data that the decompiler could not turn into code, so no further behaviour can be recovered.

name: call_stub_with_fixed_argument
description: Calls a library stub with a base-relative address and the constant two, then returns. It is called by one other routine.

name: initialize_graphics_and_load_assets
description: Large initialization routine that opens the graphics library, refers to a Graphics Error message if the open fails, and sets up base-relative state. It refers to the df0:gfx files bomben, level1, top and trenn, calls a 32-bit fixed-point multiply routine, and calls about 39 other routines.

name: update_counters_and_call_routine
description: Increments two counters, sets a flag word, adjusts two values by fixed offsets, and passes them with constant arguments to another routine. It calls three other routines and is called by one other routine.

name: update_counters_and_call_routine
description: Increments a counter from a stored value, sets a flag word, increments a second counter, passes two offset values with constant arguments to another routine, then calls it with a constant. It calls three other routines and is called by two other routines.

name: dispatch_mode_arguments
description: Chooses one of two argument sets according to the input value and a stored flag word, calls a library stub with fixed coordinates, and passes the result to a second routine. It uses the fixed-point multiply routine and is called by four other routines.

name: advance_positions_five_steps
description: Runs a five-step loop that adds velocity values to two stored positions, clears a flag word when a position leaves a fixed range, and calls library stubs to test and update the position each step. It calls four library stubs and is called by one other routine.

name: advance_position_until_bounds
description: Repeatedly moves two stored positions by their velocity values for up to five steps, stopping early when a position leaves a fixed range, and calls library stubs on each step. It calls four library stubs and is called by one other routine.

name: find_free_offset_near_point
description: Checks a point through a library stub and, when the check fails, searches a small neighbourhood of offsets for one that passes, storing the offset that is found. It calls a stub and three other routines and is called by one other routine.

name: run_state_machine_step
description: Runs a small state machine on a stored mode value: when a related flag is clear and the mode is non-zero, it runs the handler for mode one, two or three, resets the mode and calls other routines with stored positions. It uses the fixed-point multiply routine and four other routines.

name: place_flagged_markers_by_side
description: Depending on the input value, checks one of two stored flags and, when it is set, computes a fixed-point offset and passes a marker position to another routine. It uses the fixed-point multiply routine and three other routines.

name: check_and_update_neighbour_positions
description: Takes a mode value and a target position, sets a threshold count for modes one and two, then loops checking a library-tested value at the position and calling routines that update several neighbouring positions. It calls four library stubs and four other routines and is called by two other routines.

name: test_and_mark_position_pair
description: Computes a pair of positions offset from stored coordinates, calls a library stub to test the first, and when the result is below a threshold issues two further stub calls on that pair. It calls four library stubs and is called by one other routine.

name: test_and_mark_position_pair
description: Computes a pair of positions offset from stored coordinates, calls a library stub to test the first, and when the result is below a threshold issues two further stub calls on that pair. It calls four library stubs and is called by one other routine.

name: draw_sequence_with_busy_waits
description: Selects two coordinate values from a mode argument, then issues a series of drawing calls separated by busy-wait loops that count up to a fixed limit. It calls two library stubs and three other routines and is called by one other routine.

name: store_offset_rectangle_coords
description: Stores four short coordinate values derived from stored positions with fixed offsets, then calls a library stub and two other routines to position a rectangle. It is called by one other routine.

name: search_free_screen_position
description: Searches candidate screen positions in nested loops over fixed ranges, testing each with a library stub and a fixed-point multiply until one passes the threshold checks, then calls further stubs at that position. It calls four library stubs and one other routine.

name: close_all_and_report_error
description: Closes all open resources through the global base, passes its argument to a routine and then calls a final cleanup, with text for a close-all message and an error-number format. It is called by seven other routines.

name: wait_for_counter_band
description: Busy-waits on a counter until it reaches a value band, then waits until it passes a second threshold before returning. It calls one other routine in its loops and is called by seven other routines.

name: select_level_graphics_by_number
description: Selects a level number from a stored value and, for each of twelve cases, runs the setup routines with fixed coordinates for the matching gfx/levelN file. It refers to the twelve level files and calls two other routines; it is called by one other routine.

name: draw_brush_graphics_by_mode
description: Draws a set of graphics elements at fixed positions and sizes using stored coordinates, branching on a mode value. It refers to the speedbrush and tronbrush graphics files, calls about fourteen routines, and compares values with AmigaDOS hunk type codes, so some of its logic may relate to loading.

name: place_three_items_with_offsets
description: Sets two state words to one, makes setup calls with fixed coordinates, then loops over three items, placing each at a computed position using a fixed-point multiply and a library stub. It calls five other routines and one library stub and is called by one other routine.

name: call_four_element_routines
description: Calls one routine and then four others with base-relative addresses of fixed elements, then returns. It calls two other routines and is called by one other routine.

name: advance_feedback_shift_state
description: Shifts a 32-bit state word eight times, feeding back an exclusive-or of two low bits on each step, then stores the low word of the result. It makes no library calls and is called by one other routine.

name: update_bit_plane_entries
description: Iterates over a table of short values, resetting entries below a threshold to a fixed value, clears bytes in up to three bitmap planes selected by each entry's index bits, and then reduces each entry by a stored step. It is called by one other routine.

name: initialize_seventy_entry_tables
description: Loops seventy times, filling three per-entry tables with values returned by other routines, offset by fixed amounts. It calls two other routines and the fixed-point multiply routine, and is called by one other routine.

name: open_title_screen_and_load
description: Opens the title screen through the intuition library, checks the format of the gfx/titel picture, and reports an Intuition error through the text messages if the screen open fails or the picture format is wrong. It calls about eleven other routines and is called by one other routine.

name: process_sixteen_row_columns
description: Loops sixteen times over a number of columns set by a stored shift value, reads a value through two routines and passes it on with a column offset, then releases a stored handle through a library stub. It calls five other routines and one library stub.

name: open_font_library_and_font
description: Opens the diskfont library and then the font named in its data, reporting an error through the text messages if either open fails. It calls four other routines and a library stub, and the text says the font cannot be opened or the diskfont library is missing.

name: call_routine_return_zero
description: Calls one other routine and returns zero. It is referenced from data and is called by one other routine.

name: initialize_tron_text_record
description: Fills a small structure with fixed byte and pointer values, including a pointer to the text TRON, then calls a library stub with it and one other routine. It is called by one other routine.

name: call_stub_with_constant_five
description: Calls a library stub with the constant five and a base-relative address, then returns. It is called by one other routine.

name: read_chip_register_with_flag
description: Reads a 16-bit custom chip register word at an address indexed by its argument, then sets or clears bit four depending on a bit of a global value, and returns the adjusted word. It is called by three other routines.

name: call_routine_return_zero
description: Calls one other routine and returns zero. It is referenced through an address taken in the code and is called by one other routine.

name: initialize_sterne_text_record
description: Fills a small structure with fixed byte and pointer values, including a pointer to the text Sterne, then calls a library stub with it and one other routine. It is called by one other routine.

name: call_stub_with_constant_five
description: Calls a library stub with the constant five and a base-relative address, then returns. It is called by one other routine.

name: fill_sixteen_by_sixteen_table
description: Fills a sixteen-by-sixteen table by looping over both indices and storing a value read through two routines at each position, after an initial call. It calls a library stub and three other routines and is called by three other routines.

name: fill_offset_sixteen_table
description: Fills the same sixteen-by-sixteen table as its neighbour, but starts the row index at one and the column index at two, skipping the first row and the first two columns. It calls a library stub and three other routines and is called by two other routines.

name: insert_value_into_sorted_table
description: Searches a table of ten sorted entries for the insertion point of a value, shifts the lower entries down to make room, and stores the value with its fields, calling library stubs and the fixed-point multiply routine along the way. It calls about six other routines and is called by one other routine.

name: insert_value_into_sorted_table
description: Searches a table of ten sorted entries for the insertion point of a value, shifts the lower entries down to make room, and stores the value with its fields. It is called by one other routine.

name: insert_value_into_sorted_table
description: Searches a table of ten sorted entries for the insertion point of a value, shifts the lower entries down to make room, and stores the value with its fields, calling library stubs and the fixed-point multiply routine along the way. It is called by one other routine.

name: load_highscore_table_or_blank
description: Fills a ten-row by eight-column text buffer with dash characters, then opens the df0:highscores file through the dos library and reads its data into the buffer, refilling it with dashes when the read is short. It is called by one other routine.

name: load_highscore_table_or_blank
description: Fills a ten-row by eight-column text buffer with dash characters, then opens the df0:highscores file through the dos library and reads its data into the buffer, refilling it with dashes when the read is short. It is referenced through an address taken in the code and is called by one other routine.

name: read_highscore_file_with_errors
description: Fills a text buffer of highscore rows with dashes, reads the df0:highscores file through a dos library call, and shows a read-error message through the text if the read fails. It calls the fixed-point multiply routine and four other routines and is called by one other routine.

name: save_highscore_file_with_errors
description: Opens the df0:highscores file for writing through the dos library, writes the highscore buffer, and shows a write-error or not-saved message through the text if the write fails. It closes the file afterwards and is called by one other routine.

name: wait_for_status_bit_set
description: Repeatedly calls a routine with the argument two until a bit in its result is set, then returns. It calls one other routine and is called by one other routine.

name: format_score_digits_for_display
description: Formats a score value into a six-character digit buffer padded with spaces, then passes the buffer to library routines at fixed positions, using the fixed-point multiply routine along the way. It calls four library stubs and six other routines and is called by three other routines.

name: format_signed_number_string
description: Converts a number to a decimal digit string in a buffer, prefixing a minus sign for negative values and ending with a zero terminator, then passes the string to another routine. It calls three other routines and is called by one other routine.

name: reverse_string_in_place
description: Reverses the bytes of a buffer in place, using the length returned by another routine to set the bounds. It calls one other routine and is called by one other routine.

name: draw_two_numeric_labels
description: Formats two stored numbers into small text buffers and draws them with a sequence of library stub calls at fixed positions. It calls two library stubs and four other routines and is called by one other routine.

name: next_random_value_below_limit
description: Advances a stored 32-bit state with a shift-and-exclusive-or step, then returns the result reduced modulo the limit argument; with a non-positive limit it only stores a new state. It is called by three other routines.

name: load_ilbm_image_file
description: Loads an IFF ILBM picture by opening the file through dos calls and parsing the chunks named BMHD, CMAP and BODY. It calls seven other routines, is called by four other routines, and reports failures through its error paths.

name: compare_four_byte_keys
description: Compares the first four bytes of two buffers, returning zero when they all match and one otherwise. It is called by one other routine.

name: release_and_format_sound_entry
description: Releases a stored handle when one is held, then passes a second handle and a stored value to a routine and clears it, dispatching on the second argument with a special case for minus one and formatting the entry through the text format string. It calls four other routines and is called by one other routine.

name: fill_slot_values_from_stub
description: Loops over a count of four-byte slots, fetching a value through a routine and a library stub for each, storing it at a fixed offset in the slot and calling a further routine when the value is zero. It uses the fixed-point multiply routine and is called by three other routines.

name: release_nonzero_slot_handles
description: Walks a slot array whose length is given by a count byte, releasing each non-zero pointer through another routine and clearing it to zero. It is called by four other routines.

name: load_sound_sample_file
description: Loads a sound sample file for a slot by allocating memory, opening the file, examining its size and reading it into memory, and reports an error message through the text if memory, opening, examining, existence or reading fails. It calls ten other routines and is called by one other routine.

name: open_audio_device_and_slots
description: Fills two arrays of five four-byte slots with values returned by other routines, then opens the audio device through the exec library and reports an error message through the text when the open fails. It calls a library stub and four other routines and is called by one other routine.

name: configure_channel_slot
description: If the channel's flag is set, writes fixed field values and the channel's stored parameters into a slot structure and passes it to another routine. It is called by four other routines.

name: configure_channel_slot_pair
description: If the channel and a shared flag are clear, writes field values into a slot structure, passes it to another routine, then writes a second configuration with position fields when a computed threshold is met. It is called by fifteen other routines.

name: call_eight_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls eight other routines in sequence and returns. It is referenced from data and is called by one other routine.

name: clear_longword_run_and_call
description: Clears a fixed run of longwords at an offset from a stack-relative base, stores the stack address and a global value into two fields, then calls another routine. It is called by one other routine and was called from the find_max_and_prepare_buffer routine.

name: format_text_and_output
description: Sets up a character output buffer and calls a formatting routine with a byte-output callback and the stack arguments, then passes the buffer start and length to an output routine, directly or through a global flag. It is called by nine other routines.

name: buffer_byte_flush_at_limit
description: Stores one byte in an output buffer and, when the buffer reaches forty bytes, passes the buffer to an output routine and resets the pointer. It is referenced through an address taken in the code and is called by one other routine.

name: flush_output_buffer_remainder
description: Passes the bytes still held in the output buffer to an output routine, resets the buffer pointer, and returns a masked byte from a stored structure. Its address is taken in the code and it is called by one other routine.

name: examine_unrecovered_routine
description: The decompiler could not produce pseudo-code for this 49-instruction routine, so its behaviour cannot be recovered from the evidence. It calls two other routines and is called by one other routine.

name: format_printf_style_string
description: Walks a format string, copying literal characters through a callback and expanding each percent conversion into digits or text with width and sign handling, then returns the count of characters written. It calls two other routines and is called by one other routine.

name: perform_signed_division
description: Computes the sign of the result from the signs of the two inputs, calls another routine to perform the division, and negates the quotient when the result should be negative. It is called by seven other routines.

name: perform_signed_remainder
description: Computes the sign from the signs of the two inputs, calls another routine, and returns its second result, the remainder, negated when the sign is negative. It is called by seven other routines.

name: return_second_result_register
description: Calls another routine and returns the value it leaves in D1. It is called by two other routines.

name: perform_32_bit_division
description: Divides an unsigned 32-bit value by another, using direct division when the divisor fits in 16 bits and a shift-and-subtract loop otherwise, and returns the quotient and remainder together in a 64-bit result. It is called by six other routines.

name: read_until_count_or_sentinel
description: Calls another routine repeatedly, counting up to the product of two packed word values, and returns the second word when the count is reached, or zero if the routine returns minus one first. It is called by two other routines.

name: examine_unrecovered_routine
description: The decompiler could not produce pseudo-code for this 22-instruction routine, so its behaviour cannot be recovered from the evidence. It calls one other routine and is called by one other routine.

name: sweep_records_in_range
description: Repeatedly calls another routine on record addresses stepped by twenty-two bytes across a fixed base-relative range, then returns. It calls one other routine and is referenced through an address taken in the code.

name: release_flagged_record_fields
description: Calls release routines for the fields of a record whose flag bits are set, zeroes its pointer and flag fields, and returns a combined value, or minus one for a null record. It calls one other routine and is called by two other routines.

name: release_flagged_record_fields
description: Calls release routines for the fields of a record whose flag bits are set, zeroes its pointer and flag fields, and returns a combined value. It calls five other routines and is referenced through an address taken in the code.
